The provision faces opposition from some Democrats and Republicans, but has bipartisan support in Congress.

articles.title: Australia news live: Aukus nations to develop uncrewed vehicles to protect undersea cables; Hanson says she could be PM | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The United States, Australia, and Britain are collaborating under the Aukus security partnership to develop advanced payloads for uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUVs). Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth announced this new project at the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore, highlighting its focus on supporting undersea operations and maintaining a maritime advantage. The initiative is part of Pillar 2 of the Aukus pact, which aims to pool defense sector talents and bolster their presence in the Indo-Pacific region.  This collaboration is seen as a response to rising tensions with China, which opposes the partnership.

articles.title: HIV+ Syrian man gets bail; ‘his ill-health not in dispute’, says Gujarat High Court | Ahmedabad News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Gujarat High Court granted conditional bail to a Syrian man who has been detained since January, citing his deteriorating health. The court acknowledged the petitioner's HIV+ status and LGBTQ+ identity while noting that his physical and mental well-being were in "tatters" at the detention center.  The court also noted that the state did not dispute the petitioner's ill health. The man was granted bail on a personal bond of Rs.10,000 with surety of the like amount, subject to strict conditions including not leaving Gujarat and reporting to police. The court will hear the petition again on June 8th.

articles.title: If namaz on roads is wrong, all religious street celebrations should also be opposed: AIMIM chief Owaisi
articles.rephrased_article: Asaduddin Owaisi, president of the AIMIM, criticized the recent alleged attacks against Muslims across India, arguing that restrictions on religious practices like offering namaz on roads should apply equally to all religions. He claimed that festivals of every religion are also unacceptable in public spaces and questioned why certain businesses are allowed to operate during religious holidays while others are not. Owaisi asserted that India belongs to all its citizens and urged for a more balanced approach towards religious freedom and the rights of Muslims.

articles.title: Want Tatas to come back to Singur; send signal West Bengal is open for business: State BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Samik Bhattacharya, West Bengal BJP president, stated that the new government wants the Tata Group to return to Singur. Bhattacharya also emphasized the need for a comprehensive land policy to encourage industrialization, highlighting that foreign investors have largely avoided West Bengal compared to other states. He aims to restore investor confidence by attracting new investments and creating employment opportunities.

articles.title: Nike World Cup Uniforms Made of Recycled Textiles Won’t Solve Fashion Waste | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Nike, one of the world's largest apparel companies, is partnering with chemical recycling companies to produce its first elite performance apparel from 100 percent textile waste. While this initiative aims to address sustainability concerns within the fashion industry, experts caution that widespread adoption of chemically recycled clothing is not imminent.  The technology faces challenges in scaling up production and processing used clothes effectively. The current focus on industrial scrap fabric suggests a limited impact on addressing projected increases in textile production.

articles.title: Kylie Jenner Opens Up About 65-Pound Pregnancy Weight Gain

Doctors monitor weight during prenatal check-ups to ensure both mother and baby remain healthy.  She also advised against crash diets or extreme workouts after delivery and emphasized the importance of breastfeeding, light exercise, adequate sleep, and stress management for postpartum recovery.

articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, TMC national general secretary, was allegedly attacked by a crowd of locals in West Bengal's Sonarpur area while visiting families of post-poll violence victims. articles.title: Is the Ferrari Luce’s Design Really That Bad? 3 Italian Auto Experts Weigh In | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: The debut of Ferrari's first electric vehicle, the Luce, has sparked controversy. The car, priced at $650,000, features a stark departure from the brand's traditional design and has drawn criticism from former chairman Luca Cordero di Montezemolo and other industry experts.  Some designers argue that the Luce lacks emotional appeal and fails to capture Ferrari's heritage, while others believe its futuristic design is innovative. The car's unconventional styling and collaboration with Apple designer Jony Ive have also been met with mixed reactions. Despite the negative feedback, some see the Luce as a bold step towards the future of the automotive industry.

articles.title: Karnataka CM Oath: D K Shivakumar to take charge on June 3
articles.rephrased_article: D K Shivakumar, the next chief minister of Karnataka, is set to take his oath on June 3 at the Glass House in Lok Bhavan. G C Chandrashekhar, the Congress state working president, confirmed the decision and stated that a simple ceremony reflecting work and service will be held.  Chandrashekhar also announced that bus arrangements for supporters were cancelled due to fuel crisis and traffic concerns.

articles.title: Four more men freed from flooded Laos cave after 10 days; five rescued so far, two still missing | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Four men trapped in a Laos cave for ten days were successfully rescued on Saturday after water was pumped out of the cavern. Lee Kian Lie, a Malaysian rescue diver, confirmed that all four rescued individuals were in stable condition and being attended to by medical personnel.  Two men remain unaccounted for, with rescuers expressing concern about their potential survival due to the cold temperatures deep within the cave. The incident echoes the 2018 Thai youth football team rescue, prompting the involvement of international divers and volunteers from Thailand, France, Indonesia, and Australia.

articles.title: Vidyasagar Setu Closed | Vidyasagar Setu to remain closed for eight hours on Sunday for repair work - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: Kolkata Police announced an eight-hour closure of the Vidyasagar Setu bridge on Sunday, May 31st, from 6 am to 2 pm. Hooghly River Bridge Commissioners Authority will replace stay cables, holding down cables and bearings during the work.  Traffic diversions will be enforced on multiple routes leading to the bridge, with vehicles diverted to Howrah Bridge via various alternate roads. The repair work is part of ongoing maintenance for the city's second Hooghly bridge.

articles.title: Canadian man who mailed ‘suicide packets’ to US, China, UK and other countries pleads guilty; victims' parents react | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Kenneth Law, a Canadian man, pleaded guilty to 14 charges related to aiding suicide in a Newmarket, Ontario court. He admitted to shipping poison-filled "suicide packets" to over 100 individuals across several countries, including Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States.  Law's sentencing is scheduled for September, with authorities in Canada and other countries investigating more than 100 suspected suicides connected to him. The case involved 14 victims from Ontario, aged between 16 and 36, who died after consuming substances supplied by Law. Prosecutors described the tragic final moments of several victims, including those who called emergency services for help after ingesting lethal chemicals purchased from Law.  Law's actions have been condemned by families of victims and experts who believe he exploited vulnerable individuals for profit.

articles.title: AI data centres India | Now, Wall Street Journal turns spotlight on water dilemma in India’s artificial intelligence data centre rush - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and other tech giants are facing growing scrutiny over their data center projects in developing countries, including India.  Concerns about water scarcity and the displacement of local communities are raising questions about the environmental and social impact of these initiatives. The Andhra Pradesh government is offering significant subsidies to attract these companies, but residents fear long-term consequences for their livelihoods and agricultural practices. Protests have also emerged in other countries like Malaysia and Indonesia, highlighting the global debate surrounding AI development and its potential effects on water resources and rural communities.

articles.title: Do You Actually Need to Pay for Transcription Software? | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Wispr Flow, an AI-powered transcription tool, promises to write faster by talking out loud instead of typing. The tool uses AI transcription and large language models (LLMs) for post-processing, removing filler words and formatting text into complete sentences. While Wispr Flow offers a sleek interface and convenient setup, its subscription cost may be prohibitive for some users. Free alternatives like Spokenly, MacParakeet, VoiceInk, and FOSS Voquill provide similar functionality without the monthly fee.  These open-source options offer varying levels of post-processing capabilities and offline functionality, providing a range of choices for individuals seeking to explore AI-powered writing tools.

articles.title: ‘Reminder of true cost of nation’s security’: Rajnath, Yogi inaugurate naval museum in Lucknow | Lucknow News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the 'Nausena Shaurya Vatika' naval museum in Lucknow. The open-air display showcases artifacts from INS Gomati, a decommissioned ship that served for 34 years.  The museum cost Rs 19 crore to build and features weapons systems, including an AK 726 naval gun and a TU 142M maritime patrol aircraft. Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi, Chief of the Naval Staff, was also present at the inauguration. The museum aims to inspire future generations about India's defense capabilities.

articles.title: "He completely deserves it": Casemiro feels Michael Carrick deserves' Manchester United job permanently - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: Casemiro, a former Manchester United player, believes Michael Carrick deserves the permanent manager position. Carrick has overseen 10 wins and two draws in 14 games, leading the team to secure third place in the Premier League and qualification for next season's Champions League. Casemiro believes Carrick's deep connection to the club, experience as a player, and ability to turn things around make him an ideal candidate for the role.

articles.title: Liverpool sack Arne Slot a year after winning championship
articles.rephrased_article: Liverpool has parted ways with manager Arne Slot, ending his tenure after a disappointing season that saw the club finish fifth in the Premier League. The club acknowledged Slot's contributions but stated that change was necessary to move forward, citing a lack of improvement despite significant investment in new players.  The decision comes after a public fallout with star player Mohamed Salah and despite Slot's initial success in his first year at the helm.

articles.title: 'Indians and Pakistanis take our jobs': UK far-right leader’s social media post sparks row
articles.rephrased_article: Rupert Lowe, a former businessman and MP for Reform UK, launched his own far-right party, Restore Britain, following an internal rift. articles.title: West Bengal AI adoption lag | Bengal and AI: For a ‘Deep State’ to aid technological innovation - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: A recent report by OpenAI reveals that India is a leader in AI adoption, with cities like Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Delhi, and Chennai leading the way. However, West Bengal lags behind, despite having a strong talent pool and intellectual tradition. The state's lack of AI adoption raises concerns about missed opportunities and potential stagnation. articles.title: SIHM will be readied by August in Uppada: Kakinada MP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jana Sena Party Kakinada MP Tangella Uday Srinivas announced that the State Institute of Hotel Management (SIHM) in Uppada will open for academic activity by August. The construction, which has been delayed due to a lack of funds from the Centre, is reportedly 95% complete with the administrative building, academic blocks, hostel and laboratory facilities being built.  The Ministry of Tourism has released ₹12 crore for the project on a five-acre land in Uppada to offer hotel management courses and address youth unemployment in Andhra Pradesh.

articles.title: Millions of Bees Have Thrived Under a New York Cemetery for More Than a Century | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Cornell University researchers discovered a colony of 5.5 million Andrena regularis bees, also known as mining bees, in East Lawn Cemetery in Ithaca, New York. The population occupies an area of about 1.25 acres and is crucial for pollination of the region's orchards. Scientists estimated the total population to be between 3 and 8 million, highlighting the importance of protecting these solitary bee species and their nesting sites.  The researchers launched a global citizen science initiative to monitor and protect underground bee aggregations before habitat fragmentation jeopardizes their survival.

articles.title: Extremely Severe Alert on phones: Loud alarm warns of bad weather in Delhi NCR — ‘such alert for basic thunderstorm’ | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued an "Extremely Severe Alert" on Saturday evening warning of severe thunderstorms and rainfall across Delhi-NCR and other parts of India. The alert, which was sent via a cell broadcast system, was intended to warn citizens of imminent, life-threatening disasters such as cyclones and heavy rainfall. While some praised the initiative, others questioned the severity of the alert for what they considered moderate weather conditions.  The IMD also issued district-wise nowcast warnings predicting thunderstorms with gusty winds up to 100 kmph in several states.

articles.title: Delhi Government notifies recruitment rules for fine arts PGTs - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: The Delhi Government has issued new recruitment rules for 217 fine arts Post-Graduate Teacher (PGT) positions in government schools. The notification, replacing older rules from 1973 and later, introduces a direct recruitment pattern with 25% of vacancies filled by direct hiring, while the remaining 75% will be filled through promotion.  The new rules also specify that there are no desirable qualifications or experience requirements for direct recruits, who must possess a master's degree in fine arts from a recognized university and have an upper age limit of 30 years. The UPSC was consulted during the process but its involvement will not be applicable to the recruitment process.

articles.title: Karnataka CM News: Why Siddaramaiah's dethroning might hit Rahul Gandhi the worst - Karnataka News | India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress high command brokered a transition formula in Karnataka, asking Siddaramaiah to resign as Chief Minister. This move has sparked protests and discontent among supporters of the veteran OBC leader, who is viewed as a strong mass leader in the state. The decision to remove Siddaramaiah, who had built the party organizationally over two decades, could potentially hurt Rahul Gandhi's political image, particularly his efforts to consolidate support for Dalits, minorities, and backward-class voters.  The move has also been criticized as unfair to a prominent leader within the party, raising concerns about potential backlash in future elections.

articles.title: Quilts Are Better Than Sleeping Bags | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Thru-hikers and ultralight redditors have embraced quilts as a lighter and more comfortable alternative to traditional sleeping bags. Quilts lay over the sleeper like a quilt, eliminating the constricting nature of mummy bags while offering similar warmth.  They are typically made of nylon and filled with down, weighing less than sleeping bags and packing smaller. While some prefer the familiar feel of a sleeping bag, many find quilts more comfortable for those who sleep warm or move around at night. The choice between a quilt and a sleeping bag depends on individual preferences and needs.

articles.title: 'No Panthic decision can be taken in Vidhan Sabha': Akal Takht Jathedar - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: Akal Takht Jathedar Jathedar Hira Singh Gabbaria warned the Punjab government against ignoring the authority of the Akal Takht, stating that no Panthic decision can be taken in the Vidhan Sabha.  He emphasized that Sikh tradition dictates decisions should be made by the supreme religious seat and urged the Punjab government to amend the sacrilege law in accordance with Akal Takht's guidance. articles.title: Liverpool sack Arne Slot a year after winning championship

articles.title: Man holds wife captive, beats her, forces ‘murga’ punishment for 4 hours; arrested - Mumbai News | India Today

articles.title: West Bengal AI adoption lag | Bengal and AI: For a ‘Deep State’ to aid technological innovation - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: OpenAI's recent report reveals that India is a major user of Artificial Intelligence, with cities like Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Delhi, and Chennai leading the adoption. articles.title: Watch: Over 1.2 million join Cockroach Janta Party, says founder Abhijeet Dipke - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, an online movement attracting over 1.2 million members, has seen his satirical platform evolve into a platform addressing youth unemployment and exam paper leaks in India. articles.title: People defeated opposition’s politics of hatred: Punjab CM Mann on civic poll outcome - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has won over 860 of the 1,977 wards in Punjab's civic body elections, leading in many others. articles.title: In 1997, India's ocean saved the monsoon from El Nino. This year, it won't - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), a natural temperature imbalance in the Indian Ocean, typically helps India's monsoon season by pushing moisture-laden winds towards the subcontinent. El Nino, a warming of the Pacific Ocean that disrupts normal weather patterns, could lead to below-average monsoon rainfall in 2026, potentially impacting crop yields and food prices. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has already lowered its forecast for the monsoon season, predicting it will be significantly below average.

articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, former West Bengal Chief Minister, alleged that BJP leaders and a senior police officer pressured hospitals to discharge Abhishek Banerjee, TMC national general secretary, despite his serious condition after an attack in Sonarpur. articles.title: Fitness Centres in Kolkata | Zumba, pilates, pickleball and more - Kolkata’s fitness culture moves beyond dumbbells and yoga mats - Telegraph India

articles.title: US green card policy | Trump administration makes U-turn on green card policy not all applicants need to leave US to apply: Report - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) clarified that not all immigrants seeking green cards will be required to return to their home countries. Industry leaders warned that this policy could disrupt technology companies reliant on foreign professionals.

articles.title: Heavy rain, cool breeze turn Chandigarh weather pleasant; max temp drops to 25.3°C - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: Heavy rain and thunderstorms swept through Chandigarh on Saturday, bringing a dramatic end to a severe heatwave that had plagued the region. While the IMD predicts below-normal monsoon rainfall for 2026, Saturday's rain provided a welcome respite.  The weather is expected to remain cool and breezy through Sunday and Monday before returning to dry conditions from Tuesday onwards.

articles.title: CBSE OSM Coempt TCS row | CBSE on screen marking row: Rahul Gandhi says ‘rules’ bent to favour Coempt, cites TCS loss in auction - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi criticized the Modi government over the CBSE exam evaluation controversy, alleging that the board lowered technical requirements to favor COEMPT Eduteck Private Limited, a company with a poor track record. He demanded an independent judicial probe into the contract awarding process and accused the government of prioritizing its survival over student well-being.  Piyush Goyal, the Union commerce minister, countered Gandhi's claims, accusing him of "propaganda" while Dharmendra Pradhan, the Union education minister, defended the board's actions. Other prominent figures like Priyanka Chaturvedi and Mohammed Zubair have also raised concerns about potential manipulation and a coordinated campaign to promote the OSM system.

articles.title: Keychron K2 HE Concrete Edition Review: Rock-Solid Typing | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Keychron has released a concrete keyboard, featuring standard plastic keycaps. The company's latest offering is well-made and coherent, despite its unconventional material choice.  The K2 HE's drab gray case, inspired by brutalist architecture, has garnered attention for its absurdity and industrial aesthetic.

articles.title: ‘Foundation stone very soon for Jindal mega industrial park’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Industries and Commerce department secretary N. Yuvaraj directed officials to expedite the foundation stone ceremony for the JSW Industrial Park Limited in S. Kota constituency. Jindal group representatives were consulted, with the Collector assuring action after speaking with them. The initiative comes amid farmer protests alleging unfulfilled promises from the company regarding job opportunities and land allocation.

articles.title: Kashmir witnesses peaceful Eid-ul-Adha celebrations amid heightened security
articles.rephrased_article: Eid-ul-Adha was celebrated peacefully across Jammu and Kashmir with religious fervor. Tens of thousands of devotees gathered at various mosques, Eidgahs, and shrines to offer prayers amid pleasant weather conditions.  Authorities intensified security preparations across the region, deploying personnel at key intersections and public places. Major congregations were witnessed at Hazratbal shrine on the banks of Dal Lake, Eidgah Srinagar, and prominent Eidgahs and Jamia Masjids in districts including Budgam, Anantnag, Baramulla, Shopian, Pulwama, Kupwara, and Bandipora.  The festival passed off peacefully without any major untoward incidents reported from any part of the Valley.

articles.title: Well-Known Educationists Arrested For Plotting Lawyer's Murder In Hyderabad | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Mujahid Alam Khan and his father Mahaboob Alam Khan, owners of educational institutions in Hyderabad, have been arrested for the murder of senior advocate Khaja Moizuddin.  The investigation revealed that long-standing disputes between the families over Waqf properties management issues led to a grudge against the deceased. The accused conspired with associates Hassan Ali alias Chaous and Muneer to hire Kishan alias Pappu who carried out the plan, resulting in Moizuddin's death outside his home.  The police commissioner stated that the Khans believed their legal setbacks were due to the deceased’s involvement in several legal proceedings against them.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Murder of a lawyer due to property disputes raises concerns about justice and safety.

articles.title: Orissa HC Quashes Action Against Vigilance Judge, Orders Restoration Of Benefits | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: The Orissa High Court has quashed disciplinary proceedings and punishment against senior judicial officer Lalit Kumar Dash. The court found the findings against Dash based on presumptions and not backed by evidence.  The bench, comprising Justices Manash Ranjan Pathak and Sibo Sankar Mishra, ordered the restoration of all consequential service benefits to Dash before his retirement in July 2026.

articles.title: Woman doctor of Dera Bassi hospital 'attacked' by 2 men; staff suspend OPD services in protest - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: A woman doctor, Jot Noor, an anaesthetist at the Dera Bassi Sub-Divisional Hospital, was attacked by two unidentified men on Friday morning. The attack occurred after she was questioned about her profession and subsequently assaulted.  Dr Noor filed a complaint with the police, and hospital staff suspended outpatient services in protest of what they described as inaction from authorities and lack of security measures. Dr Dharminder Singh, the Dera Bassi Sub-Divisional Officer (SMO), confirmed a police complaint was filed and a case registered.

articles.title: Truck plunges into gorge at Zojila Pass; driver, conductor escape miraculously
articles.rephrased_article: A truck driver and his conductor escaped uninjured after their 14-wheeler truck plunged into a deep gorge near Zojila on the Srinagar-Leh highway. The accident occurred near Pani Matha in the Zojila sector, when the truck lost control before skidding off the road.  The truck was completely damaged, but both the driver and conductor were unharmed. Police and local authorities responded to the scene to investigate the cause of the incident.

articles.title: Hegseth: America Prepared To Resume Iran Attacks If Agreement Not Reached | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned that the United States is prepared to resume aerial attacks on Iran if diplomatic efforts fail.  He stated that the US has sufficient munitions and can handle multiple conflicts simultaneously, emphasizing President Trump's commitment to securing a nuclear-free Iran. A 60-day truce extension is being negotiated, with both sides working towards a permanent end to the conflict. The war, launched in February, has resulted in thousands of casualties and global economic strain due to Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Reshwari emerges as popular tourist retreat in Kupwara
articles.rephrased_article: Reshwari, a scenic destination in the foothills of Bangus Valley, has become increasingly popular among locals and tourists. Visitors are drawn to the gushing waters of Nallah Mawer, offering cool breezes and prime trout fishing opportunities.  The Forest Department's Langate Division maintains a rest house at Reshwari, providing accommodation and food facilities for visitors. Locals have reported an increase in tourist footfall, contributing positively to local economic growth.

articles.title: Indian football team gets rousing diaspora welcome in UK
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian men's football team received a warm welcome from the Indian diaspora in London ahead of their third-place match against Zimbabwe. Deputy High Commissioner Kartik Pande welcomed the players, emphasizing the unifying power of sports and highlighting India's progress in football. Kalyan Chaubey, president of the All India Football Federation (AIFF), also spoke about the importance of bilateral ties between India and the UK, particularly in fostering cooperation for football development. The team urged fans to support them at their final Unity Cup match.

articles.title: UAE Carried Out Dozens Of Strikes Against Iran With Support From US And Israel: Report | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) allegedly carried out dozens of airstrikes against Iran with support from the US and Israel, according to a report in The Wall Street Journal. The strikes began early in the war and continued until the April ceasefire, suggesting a deeper involvement than previously known.  The UAE targeted Iranian energy facilities in response to Tehran's attacks on their oil and gas infrastructure, including the Asaluyeh petrochemical complex.  The strikes were coordinated with the US and Israel, who provided intelligence.

articles.title: 100 Days Nasha Mukt J&K Abhiyan | Paddar Premier League Cricket Tournament begins in Kishtwar
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Commissioner Kishtwar, Pankaj Kumar Sharma, inaugurated the Paddar Premier League 2026 Cricket Tournament at Chhatargarh Stadium. The event was organized by the local administration in collaboration with the Department of Youth Services & Sports, Kishtwar, and other stakeholders.  Sharma encouraged youth participation in sports for personal development as part of the ongoing "100 Days Nasha Mukt Jammu & Kashmir Abhiyan." He also held a public grievance redressal meeting and inspected pilgrimage arrangements for the Shri Machail Mata Ji Yatra 2026. The event was attended by ADC Kishtwar Pawan Kotwal, SDM Paddar Dr. Amit Kumar, SDPO Paddar Vijay Bhagat, Tehsildar Paddar Vijay Gupta, and other officers.

articles.title: NMBA: DYSS holds sports activities in Rajouri
articles.rephrased_article: Department of Youth Services & Sports, Rajouri, organized sports and awareness activities as part of the "Nasha Mukt Jammu & Kashmir Abhiyan" in various zones of District Rajouri. The events included cricket and volleyball matches, training sessions, and orientation programs aimed at promoting fitness, discipline, teamwork, and a drug-free lifestyle among youth.  The initiatives witnessed enthusiastic participation from players and spectators, reflecting growing awareness and positive engagement with constructive activities.

articles.title: 8 Held After Violent Clash Inside Police Station In Odisha's Baripada | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Baripada Town police responded to a violent clash between two groups of youths at the police station on Friday evening.  The incident, which involved vandalism and assault, led to the arrest of eight individuals for their involvement in the altercation. Police sources said that the clash stemmed from an argument between youths from Baripada and Dhanpur areas over a car ride.

articles.title: Eid-ul-Adha celebrated with religious fervour across Jammu
articles.rephrased_article: Eid-ul-Adha was celebrated with religious fervor and communal harmony across the Jammu region, with thousands of devotees gathering at mosques and Eidgahs to offer prayers for peace, prosperity, and well-being. Deputy Commissioners, along with senior officers from the civil and police administrations, extended greetings to the Muslim community and visited major congregational sites.  MLA Arjun Singh Raju of Ramban district greeted the people on Eid-ul-Adha, while SSP Arun Gupta and other senior officers were also present. The celebrations passed off peacefully amidst elaborate security arrangements and festive spirit.

articles.title: Muted Celebrations For RCB Fans In Bengaluru Even If Team Wins; Restrictions By Police | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru City Police issued an advisory urging the public to avoid celebrations and disturbances after the IPL 2026 final on May 31st, following a tragic stampede in 2025 that resulted from fan celebrations. The advisory prohibits bursting firecrackers, road celebrations, large gatherings, and the use of dangerous materials. The police also urged people to maintain peace and discipline, follow traffic instructions, avoid consuming alcohol in public places, and refrain from engaging in fights or indecent behavior.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Restrictions on celebrations after a tragic event raise concerns about overreach.

articles.title: New Punjab BJP chief Kewal Dhillon won’t be able to deliver: Capt Amarinder - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: Capt Amarinder Singh, former Punjab Chief Minister, criticized the appointment of Kewal Dhillon as the new BJP state chief, arguing that organizational capability should have been prioritized over caste considerations.  He expressed concern about the BJP's lack of a strong base in Punjab and suggested an alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) for electoral success. He also criticized the Aam Aadmi Party government's centralized control and highlighted the state's economic challenges, security concerns, and political instability.

articles.title: Govt committed to responsive governance, grassroots development: Deputy CM
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary conducted a tour of Nowshera, inspecting developmental projects and healthcare facilities. He met with delegations and individuals to address public issues and concerns. During his visit to the Sub-District Hospital Nowshera, Choudhary assessed patient care and directed authorities to improve healthcare services.  He also reviewed ongoing works at the Dak Bunglow Nowshera, emphasizing the need for timely completion and quality standards.

articles.title: Rajouri Encounter Day 7: More reinforcement rushed to encounter site
articles.rephrased_article: The ongoing Indian Army operation, "Operation Sheruwali," in the Dori Maal area of Rajouri district, Jammu and Kashmir, has entered its seventh consecutive day.  Security forces have intensified their efforts to neutralize two suspected terrorists hiding in the dense forest area, with intermittent gunfire and explosions reported from the encounter site. Forces have deployed additional reinforcements and maintained a tight cordon around the forest, while round-the-clock surveillance is being conducted.

articles.title: Over 45000 BLOs Fan Out As Door-To-Door SIR Survey Begins In Odisha | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India in Odisha began a comprehensive Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls on Saturday, involving 45,255 Booth Level Officers (BLOs). The process aims to ensure the accuracy of voter lists ahead of future elections. BLOs are visiting households to distribute enumeration forms and assist voters with updating their details.  The SIR will continue until June 28th, with officials requesting all eligible Indian citizens to be included in the voter list while removing ineligible entries. Political parties have been asked to appoint Booth Level Agents (BLAs) for every polling station to ensure transparency. The draft electoral roll will be published on July 5th, and claims and objections can be filed until September 2nd.

articles.title: Congress move to bring Girish Chodankar back to helm Goa unit sparks discontent | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Congress appointed Girish Chodankar as the new Goa Pradesh Congress Committee (GPCC) president, replacing Amit Patkar. This move has sparked discontent among some party leaders who question Chodankar's 2022 performance in Goa and his appointment after a three-year absence from the post.  Patkar, who skipped the event where Chodankar took charge, is reportedly planning to form a new political party with his supporters. The AICC has also appointed three new state working presidents: M K Shaikh, Altone D’Costa, and Carlos Alvares Ferreira.

articles.title: CBSE To Make Answer Scripts Available For Students Through DigiLocker | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: The Union education ministry is planning a full audit of the Central Board of Secondary Education's (CBSE) on-screen marking system (OSM), from tendering to implementation, following concerns about glitches and evaluation issues.  This comes after students raised questions about answer sheet access, discrepancies in scanned copies, and technical glitches during re-evaluation. The company chosen for the OSM work, Coempt Edu Teck, is based in Telangana and has faced allegations regarding its previous work in the state.

articles.title: Bengal News: TMC-allied Tollywood actor Parambrata Chatterjee gets arrest shield as Rograni post bites back - West Bengal News | India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Actor Parambrata Chatterjee and actress Swastika Mukherjee are facing legal action for social media posts made in 2021 following the West Bengal Assembly elections. The posts, which included a call to "declare World 'Rograni Dibosh' Day," have resurfaced after the BJP won the recent state election, leading to an FIR filed against them.  Chatterjee and Mukherjee are accused of inciting violence by their comments, with authorities citing sections of the Indian Penal Code that pertain to incitement and promoting enmity between groups. Chatterjee sought anticipatory bail from the Calcutta High Court, which granted it for four weeks pending investigation. The case has drawn criticism from BJP leaders who accuse Chatterjee of political opportunism, while some critics have labeled him a "chameleon" for shifting his allegiances.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Potential abuse of power by filing charges for old social media posts after a political shift.

articles.title: Japanese proverb of the day: Money grows on the tree of persistence' | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: A Japanese proverb, "Money grows on the tree of persistence," emphasizes that financial success is often achieved through sustained effort rather than instant gratification. The proverb compares wealth to fruit growing on a tree, suggesting that long-term commitment and consistent hard work are essential for achieving significant results. This message is particularly relevant for students, entrepreneurs, and professionals working towards their goals, reminding them that patience and consistency matter more than talent alone.

articles.title: Aam Aadmi Party scores big in Punjab civic elections - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) secured a resounding victory in Punjab's urban local body elections, winning control of five municipal corporations and nine nagar panchayats.  Bhagwant Mann, the Chief Minister, hailed the outcome as "historic" and attributed it to AAP's model of good governance. The party also performed strongly in 19 nagar panchayats, securing a majority in most areas. Manish Sisodia, AAP Punjab affairs in-charge, emphasized the landslide victory as a testament to the people's endorsement of their model.  The Congress finished second, while Independents secured third place.

articles.title: Haryana government has assured to maintain 1,000 cusecs of water supply through Munak Canal: Delhi CM | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Haryana Chief Minister Rekha Gupta assured that the state will supply 1,000 cusecs of water to Delhi daily through the Munak Canal.  The Delhi Jal Board (DJB) is currently producing around 900-924 cusecs of water per day, but faces a shortfall of over 300 MGD during peak summer. The DJB has been working to maintain production and ensure minimal disruption for residents, while also addressing complaints related to water scarcity. Water Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh highlighted the challenges posed by the low Yamuna water level at Wazirabad Barrage, but emphasized efforts to sustain water production.  The CM directed officials to address all water leakage complaints and deploy more tankers in affected areas.

articles.title: Abhishek Banerjee heckled | TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee allegedly manhandled by agitating locals at Sonarpur in Bengal's South 24 Parganas: Police - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, Trinamool Congress national general secretary, was physically attacked by a mob in Sonarpur, West Bengal, while visiting families of post-poll violence victims.  The incident occurred after he arrived to meet the family of Sanju Karmakar, a victim of the violence.  Local residents shouted "thief" slogans and hurled objects at him. Derek O'Brien, leader of Trinamool in Rajya Sabha, condemned the attack and called for action from the police. Opposition leaders across parties, including Samik Bhattacharya (BJP), Mallikarjun Kharge (Congress), Akhilesh Yadav (SP), Arvind Kejriwal (AAP), and Tejashwi Yadav (RJD), condemned the attack on Banerjee and called for an end to political violence.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Physical assault on a political leader by a mob raises concerns about law and order.

articles.title: Reshuffle in Udhampur Police, SHOs, officers transferred
articles.rephrased_article: District Police Udhampur has ordered the transfer and posting of several officers with immediate effect. Inspector Purshotam Kumar was transferred from Rehmbal to Ramnagar, while Inspector Nishant Gupta moved from DPL Udhampur to Chenani.  Inspector Parvez Sajad, currently at DPL Udhampur, will assume charge as SHO of Udhampur after the relieving of the current officer, Abhijeet Sirohi. Other transfers include Inspector Sumit Magotra moving to Rehmbal and PSI Manveer Singh being transferred from Ramnagar to Udhampur.  PSI Varun Sharma has been moved to Battal Ballian as Incharge Police Post, while PSI Ravinder Kumar was transferred from Battal Ballian to Udhampur. The transfers are intended to improve the administration and efficiency of the police department across the district.

articles.title: 7 dead as car gets crushed between two container trucks in Pune
articles.rephrased_article: Seven people were killed and over a dozen injured in a horrific accident on the Mumbai-Bengaluru Highway in Pune city. A car became trapped between two container trucks that caught fire after one lost control due to a suspected brake failure, according to Deputy Commissioner of Police Sambhaji Kadam.  Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar, who visited the scene, said the fire erupted due to the impact of the collision. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced ₹5 lakh ex-gratia for the families of the deceased.

articles.title: India Preparing For Operation Sindoor 2.0: Army Chief | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: General Upendra Dwivedi, the Chief of Army Staff, stated that India is preparing for a potential second phase of Operation Sindoor. He emphasized that while the current situation is a temporary cessation of hostilities, the Indian military, including the Air Force and Navy, remains prepared should a fresh operation be necessary.  Dwivedi highlighted the importance of information warfare in uniting the nation behind a common narrative to ensure victory. India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7, 2025, following a terror attack in Pahalgam, Kashmir, which escalated into missile and drone strikes by Pakistan against Indian targets.

articles.title: Keychron K2 HE Concrete Edition Review: Rock-Solid Typing | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Keychron has released a concrete keyboard, featuring a gray case and standard plastic keycaps. The company's latest product aims to bridge the gap between industrial aesthetics and functional design, offering a well-made and coherent typing experience despite its unconventional material.  The K2 HE keyboard is generating buzz for its unique construction and serves as a conversation starter with its stark appearance.

articles.title: Odisha Gymnastics Apologises After Dead President's Name On Letterhead Sparks Row | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Ashok Kumar Sahoo, secretary of the Odisha Gymnastics Association, apologized for continuing to use the late president Samir Dey's name on official letterheads.  Sahoo acknowledged an oversight error and stated that the association is working to rectify it. A complaint has questioned how the OGA secured nearly Rs 98 lakh from the state government for the 2026 National Gymnastics Championships while invoices exceeding Rs 1.96 crore continued to bear Dey's name as president.

articles.title: Industry stakeholders seek balanced expansion of J&K industrial package ahead of high-level review
articles.rephrased_article: Industry stakeholders and experts have expressed concerns about the New Central Sector Scheme (NCSS) for J&K, highlighting a need for a more balanced approach to industrial growth. They suggest that the scheme's current focus on select pockets with better infrastructure could lead to uneven distribution of investments and employment opportunities across the 20 districts of the Union Territory.  They also emphasize the importance of addressing existing industrial units' challenges through revival programs, market support for local enterprises, and a more inclusive policy framework that supports both new and existing businesses. The upcoming review meeting on May 30th is expected to address these concerns and strengthen the industrial policy framework in J&K.

articles.title: Dr Jitendra to inaugurate ‘Lavender festival’ at Bhaderwah on June 6: Director CSIR-IIIM Jammu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State in the PMO, will inaugurate the 4th Lavender festival organized by CSIR-Indian Institute of Integrative Medicine (IIIM), Jammu. The festival, themed "Lavender goes global," celebrates the success of lavender cultivation and rural entrepreneurship in J&K.  The event, under the mentorship of Dr Jitendra Singh and guidance of Dr N Kalaiselvi, Director General CSIR and Secretary DSIR, will feature startup exhibitions, live demonstrations, and technical sessions on lavender cultivation and aroma-based products. The festival aims to promote agri-based entrepreneurship, sustainable livelihoods, and innovation in the aromatic crops sector.

articles.title: Cyclone Ditwah leaves 366 dead in Sri Lanka; rain alert in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry
articles.rephrased_article: Cyclone Ditwah, which has weakened into a deep depression, continues to hover near the Tamil Nadu and Puducherry coasts. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M K Stalin held a review meeting with district collectors to assess the situation, while the Greater Chennai Corporation deployed 103 boats for rescue operations. The IMD predicts further rainfall in the region, leading to disruptions in normal life and damage to crops. Sri Lanka announced a special public-private fund to support recovery efforts after the devastating floods and landslides caused by Cyclone Ditwah, resulting in a death toll of 366 with 367 people still missing. International assistance is pouring in from countries like the UK, China, Australia, and Nepal.

articles.title: Eye on poll, BJP picks Kewal Singh Dhillon as first Jat Sikh Punjab unit chief - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP appointed Kewal Singh Dhillon as the new president of its Punjab unit, a move seen as an attempt to broaden the party's appeal beyond its Hindu-based image.  Dhillon, a Jat Sikh leader with experience in both Congress and BJP, is expected to focus on farmers' welfare and ensure minimum support price (MSP) for crops. The BJP hopes Dhillon will help them gain power in the 2027 Assembly elections. While Sunil Jakhar, who previously held the position, has not been assigned a new role yet, sources suggest he will remain influential in the party's Punjab campaign.

articles.title: After SCO summit drive, Modi, Putin share car ride again as Russian president begins 27-hour India visit | India News
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin, the Russian president, arrived in New Delhi for a 27-hour visit aimed at strengthening an enduring partnership with India.  The visit, which includes meetings and events focused on trade, defense, and energy cooperation, follows a shared car ride between Modi and Putin after the SCO summit. The two leaders are expected to discuss a range of issues, including India's widening trade deficit with Russia and potential collaboration on small modular reactors.  The visit is significant as it comes amidst strained relations between India and the United States.

articles.title: No ‘double standards’ in fight against terrorism: NSA Doval in Russia
articles.rephrased_article: Ajit Doval, National Security Advisor of India, called for decisive action against terrorism and a rejection of double standards in the fight against it during an international security forum in Russia.  He emphasized the need for reforms to existing structures and institutions established after World War II, ensuring greater representation from the Global South.  Doval also highlighted the importance of safe and uninterrupted trade through critical shipping routes like the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, particularly given ongoing conflicts in West Asia. During his visit to Russia, Doval met with Sergei Shoigu, Secretary of the Security Council of the Russian Federation, to discuss defense, security, energy, and trade-economic ties.  The meeting also served as an opportunity to exchange views on preparations for the upcoming BRICS national security advisers' meeting in New Delhi.

articles.title: Permanent Hormuz Transit Fees To Hit Consumers, Temporary Tolls Negotiable: Qatar | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Qatar's Deputy Prime Minister, Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, rejected the idea of a permanent legal levy on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, stating it would ultimately impact consumers. He suggested temporary charges for specific needs like mine-clearing operations could be negotiable.  Sheikh Saoud also emphasized Qatar's desire to maintain diplomatic ties with Iran and called for a unified response from the Gulf Cooperation Council in dealing with Iranian actions.

articles.title: US, China trade journalist expulsions days after Trump visits Xi in Beijing
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration revoked the visa of a Chinese national working for Xinhua, in response to Beijing's expulsion of a New York Times reporter. This reciprocal action follows China's decision to expel Vivian Wang, a China correspondent for the newspaper, over the appearance of Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te in a recorded interview at a DealBook Summit. The move has raised concerns among other Western media who might interview Lai and risk losing their reporting abilities within China.  The US State Department previously designated some major Chinese news groups as "foreign missions" and limited visas for journalists working for US media.

articles.title: India is 'powerful' and 'modernising' its military, says Hegseth
articles.rephrased_article: Pete Hegseth, US Secretary of War, stated that India is modernizing its military with heavy industrial and logistics capabilities to support high-end operations.  He also emphasized the importance of co-production between the US and India as part of a national manufacturing globalisation of defense. Hegseth discussed the US's defense strategy in the Asia-Pacific region, highlighting its role in maintaining regional security and calling for increased investment in defense by nations globally.  The Shangri-La Dialogue brought together top officials from 44 countries.

articles.title: Nine Nabbed For Links With ISI, Dawood; Had Planned Strikes On Sensitive Locations | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi Police arrested nine men with links to Pakistan’s ISI, Dawood Ibrahim, and an al-Qaeda-affiliated group, Ansar Ghazwat-ul-Hind. The suspects were planning attacks in Delhi, Mumbai, and other parts of the country, including targeting vital installations and security personnel.  The arrests followed a period of surveillance and officials are investigating possible cross-border linkages, funding channels, and overseas handlers.

articles.title: Many, possibly students, feared trapped as building collapses in Delhi's Saket | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: A five-storey building collapsed near Saket metro station in Delhi on Saturday evening, trapping several people under debris.  The Delhi Fire Services (DFS) responded to the incident and deployed seven fire tenders, while police launched a search and rescue operation. The building housed a coaching institute on the ground floor and construction work was underway on upper floors. Residents are assisting with the rescue efforts, and authorities have not yet confirmed the number of people trapped.

articles.title: India signs BrahMos missile deal with Vietnam, nears pact with Indonesia | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Rajesh Kumar Singh, India's Defence Secretary, confirmed that an agreement to supply BrahMos cruise missiles to Vietnam has been officially executed.  Singh also stated that a parallel defense contract with Indonesia is nearing completion. He emphasized that India prioritizes sharing advanced defense technologies with trusted strategic allies, particularly within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). This move signifies India's growing influence in Southeast Asia as it strengthens its defense diplomacy and seeks to cultivate reliable alliances and secure maritime domains.

articles.title: TMC panchayat member promises to return cut money, villagers blare reminders on loudspeakers - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Villagers in West Bengal's Cooch Behar district are using loudspeakers to remind a Trinamool Congress (TMC) leader, Jyotsna Barman, of a promised refund for "cut money" collected from beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana.  The villagers allege that they were forced to pay commissions ranging from Rs 5,000 to Rs 25,000 to secure benefits and avoid delays in future installments during the previous TMC regime. The deadline for returning the "cut money" is June 4th, and residents have threatened fresh protests if the promise is not kept.

articles.title: How Iran's Hardliners Are Trying To Sabotage A Peace Deal With US
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's hard-line faction, including members of Parliament and the Supreme National Security Council, is opposing a potential US deal with Iran, using rallies and media to resist compromise.  The opposition argues against any negotiation terms, despite calls for unity from President Masoud Pezeshkian. State TV has been criticized for biased coverage against the talks, deepening political rifts within the country. Ali Bagheri Kani, a hard-line politician who serves as deputy secretary of the National Security Council, attempted to undermine negotiators by urging Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei to impose limits on the team. Despite internal disagreements, Khamenei continues to support the negotiating team.

articles.title: Indian citizenship proof: Can you prove your Indian citizenship? I'm not sure I can - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The author reflects on the complexities of proving Indian citizenship, highlighting the lack of a definitive document.  Despite having various documents like identity cards and voter IDs, they are unable to definitively prove their citizenship status. The author compares this situation to God's non-citizen status, emphasizing the ambiguity surrounding citizenship in India. They argue that while there are numerous definitions and documents claiming the opposite, there is no single document proving Indian citizenship. This lack of clarity highlights a frustrating paradox within the Indian legal system.

articles.title: Pete hegseth US Iran War Trump Aide Warns US "More Than Capable" Of Restarting Iran War
articles.rephrased_article: The United States warned it is capable of restarting the war with Iran after President Donald Trump stated his red lines for any potential peace deal, including preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons. President Trump and US Central Command (CENTCOM) have signaled continued vigilance in the region while Iran's IRNA state news agency reported Iranian air defenses shot down a drone belonging to the US-Zionist aggressor enemy. Despite ongoing diplomatic efforts, including attempts to stop fighting in Lebanon, competing conditions remain as Iran demands the release of $12 billion before moving forward with negotiations and Trump insists on Iran removing mines from the Strait of Hormuz and ending its closure.

articles.title: From gambling on rains to exchange-traded rain futures, a full circle for Mumbai - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange Limited (NCDEX) will launch India's first weather derivatives on June 1st, based on rainfall deviation data from the India Meteorological Department (IMD). This follows a historical trend of rain-gambling in Mumbai during the late 19th century, where bets were placed on rainfall patterns and their impact on daily life.  The practice was eventually curtailed by authorities but continued to evolve into new forms of gambling like cotton price speculation and later, matka.
